newsitem.title: INDIA: India signs deals for 300,000 tonnes soymeal sales.
newsitem.headline: India signs deals for 300,000 tonnes soymeal sales.

text.p: India has contracted to export nearly 300,000 tonnes of soymeal for November, December and January shipments, traders said on Friday.
They said demand for Indian soymeal in China was increasing since freight costs from Indian ports were cheaper compared with other exporting countries.
Traders said Indian soymeal was preferred since it contained 48 percent protein compared to 44 percent in soymeal from other origins.
Indian exporters were currently signing contracts at $282-283 per tonne FAS. Prices for ready shipments were quoted at $302-303 per tonne, traders said.
"An upward trend in soymeal prices would increase as sellers were reluctant," said Anuradha Ratnparkhi, a leading oilmeal exporter.
"Malaysia has also come forward to buy Indian soymeal. Sellers are few due to uncertainty over the soybean crop," she said.
She said rains were needed in the later part of September for a good soybean crop.
Traders said Singapore-based Peter Cremer had bought 100,000 tonnes, Germany's Toepfer International 60,000 tonnes, and Hong Kong based Concordia, 40,000 tonnes.
Details of the remaining deals were not available.
The main Indian sellers were OILFED, Gujarat Ambuja Protein Ltd and Prestige Foods Ltd.
